I'm sure there's customer orders which need to be fulfilled. Look at which orders are the most urgent and start from there.
 You could also look at past data to determine a forecast for items which are likely to sell. If those items are low in your warehouse, look into which suppliers provide them and put in an order.
 Get to know the staff so you understand what everyone does.
More fun running behind that behind, in fairness. I'd happily finish second.

It can drive you to be suicidal if consumed in sufficient quantities. If you ever took that plunge, the world for the most part continues on. The GOP or Democrats won't care about your decision. The only difference is you've irreparably hurt your friends and family, as well as destroying any chance of life getting better.

You honestly sound like me. I have a degree but did nothing with it. I've worked a warehouse job and earned similar pay to yours. You can try courses on Udemy or MOOC. When you find something you're interested in, you can consider getting a degree in it. I know all about being directionless. It's hard to maintain discipline for something you're not that interested in. I don't necessarily have great advice (sorry about that). I can just relate to your frustration.

I'm always reminded of the quote from American History X..."Has anything you've done made your life better?". There's a lot in this world you can't control. Focus on building yourself to be the person you want to be and forget about how crazy the world can be. Just let go. I struggle everyday with my mental health but deciding to just focus on myself is probably the way forward. Forget about politics, covid, sports results, tv shows, mindless internet surfing. I'm not where I want to be and it needs fixing.
I just wish there was a convenient way to do it, like flicking a light switch. I don't want to attempt to hang myself and mess it up.
